display_name: Paul, companion of Andrew of Mesopotamia

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Πέτρος, Διονύσιος, Ανδρέας, Παύλος, Χριστίνα, Ηράκλειος, Παυλίνος και Βενέδιμος οι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off; the life page carries «Αγιος Παυλος ο Μαρτυρας» as its own head name.

Read out of the heading of the Охридски пролог’s second entry for 18. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Петар, Дионисије, Андреј, Павле и Христина.“ — Свети is not a rank and мученици the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, so the heading leaves five bare forenames and the body adds nothing to any of them but a description. Measured with `foldchk.py` before drafting: `[('paul-companion-of-quadratus', 'sr'), ('paul-of-jamnia', 'sr'), ('paul-of-ptolemais', 'sr')]`. The folds are read in this batch’s commit message.

death.note: saint.gr: «Όλοι αυτοί οι Άγιοι μαρτύρησαν στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)» — the page gives no year, only that reign, and the bracket is the reign.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Πέτρος, Διονύσιος, Ανδρέας, Παύλος, Χριστίνα, Ηράκλειος, Παυλίνος και Βενέδιμος οι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Eight head names on one page, so eight folders**, which is `docs/CORPUS.md` §10.1 — and the corpus already keeps four of the eight, so this is one of four new folders and four upgrades from the same page. **The company's apolytikion names all eight and is copied whole**, «Παυλῖνον Διονύσιον καὶ Πέτρον ὁμοῦ, Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Βενέδιμον, τὸν θεόφρονα Παῦλον, Ἡράκλειον τὸν ἔνδοξον, καὶ Χριστίναν τὴν θείαν», with the kontakion beside it; both are the company's own and neither is a mis-hang. **The display name distinguishes him by his companion and his country**, the corpus keeping several Pauls and the page giving him nothing but «ο Μάρτυρας»: he and Andrew were of Mesopotamia, soldiers of Decius, who became soldiers of Christ at Athens and were stoned with Dionysius and Christina. **`soldier` is in `types`** on that. **No `locations` object**, although Mesopotamia and Athens are named. **The page's couplet for the three stoned men is quoted in the life.**

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 31.05.2026 (18. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Петар, Дионисије, Андреј, Павле и Христина.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 18/5 the Greek row already carries. **A YEAR READ AND REFUSED BECAUSE IT WOULD NARROW.** „То је било 250. године“ gives **250**, and this folder’s `death` already holds the wider interval its own source gave — so writing 250 would narrow a sourced interval, which the coordinator’s ruling forbids. `dates` is **untouched** and the Prologue is recorded here as a book that puts the year inside that bracket. **Two of this company got a first date from this entry and three did not, and the difference is only which folders already carried an interval** — `peter-of-lampsacus` and `dionysius-of-lampsacus` had no `dates` object at all. **New here**: that the Prologue calls him a soldier, and above all **the end of Nicomachus**, which no other book read for this company carries: „одрече се Христа усред мука, и наедном сиђе с ума, па као бесан гризаше своје тело и бацаше пену на уста докле не издахну“ — he denied Christ in the middle of the tortures, went out of his mind at once, and gnawed his own flesh and foamed at the mouth until he expired. `peter-of-lampsacus`’s life already records the denial off doxologia; **the madness and the death are this book’s**. **Nicomachus gains no folder and no row**: he is an apostate and no calendar read for this corpus keeps him, `ls saints | grep -iE 'nicomach'` returns nothing, and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for him. `types` untouched. No `locations`; this entry names no place at all, where the Romanian has Lampsacus and the Greek has Athens. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Τῶν ἀθλοφόρων τὸν ὀκτάριθμον δῆμον, μαρτυρικοὶς ἐγκωμιάσωμεν ὕμνοις, Παυλῖνον Διονύσιον καὶ Πέτρον ὁμοῦ, Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Βενέδιμον, τὸν θεόφρονα Παῦλον, Ἡράκλειον τὸν ἔνδοξον, καὶ Χριστίναν τὴν θείαν οὗτοι καὶ γὰρ πρεσβεύουσιν ἀεί, ὑπὲρ τοῦ κόσμου. Χριστῷ τῷ θεῷ ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ὃ ὑψωθεῖς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ, on the page of the eight martyrs of 18 Μαΐου

english.text: Let us praise with martyrs' hymns the eight-numbered company of the victors: Paulinus, Dionysius and Peter together, Andrew and Benedimus, God-minded Paul, glorious Heraclius and divine Christina; for these intercede always for the world with Christ our God.

hymns.text: Διαφόρων πόλεων ἐξωρμημένοι, οὐρανίου πόλεως, πολῖται ὢφθητε σεπτοί, χορόν λαμπρόν συγκροτήσαντες Μάρτυρες θεῖοι, Τριάδος ὑπέρμαχοι.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον, on the page of the eight martyrs of 18 Μαΐου

english.text: Setting out from different cities, you were shown to be honoured citizens of the heavenly city, forming one bright choir, divine martyrs, champions of the Trinity.
